messages.body:
DIRECTIVE — Alex, 2026-08-25. MANAGER LOOP. Design and build. This is the role that has been missing all day.

WHY: today the loop ran every pass and landed 4 tickets in 22h. Nothing was watching the STATS — only individual gates watching individual tickets. Alex found it, not the machine. A manager loop is the thing whose job is the numbers, every minute, and whose output is a DEMAND for data when the numbers are not in front of it.

ROLE — the manager does not build. It watches, demands, and fronts.
1) EVERY MINUTE it reads the counters: claimed vs max_concurrent, done-in-last-hour, failures per stage per cause, oldest unclaimed age, spend, distinct spec questions open, bridge volume.
2) DEMANDS THE DATA. A counter that is missing, stale, or the same shape on a healthy pass as on an empty one (BEB-2690 §3 — this is firing right now, 3× today) is itself the red. The manager does not wait for a red to be filed; the ABSENCE of fresh numbers IS the red. It demands the emitting service report per pass, by name.
3) FRONTS. It can raise weight to 10 and put an item at the head of the queue, same convention as CODE RED, recorded with a timestamp and the reason. That is its authority.

WHAT IT TRACKS: 15 medium-range goals concurrently. Per goal, already pre-rendered in state per BEB-3575 — weight, name, landed/total, countdown or OVERDUE +Nh, last landed evidence timestamp. The manager's specific job is the DERIVATIVE, not the level: a goal whose last landed evidence has not moved in N hours is red even if its counts look fine. A fenced chain that goes quiet is silence, not progress.

STRUCTURE: this is the Plan-and-Execute layer we do not have. The build loop is ReAct — one thought/action/observation per pass, no memory, so it re-derives from zero forever (that is today's root cause). The manager is the layer above it that holds the plan, holds the state, and notices that 560 attempts at one cause is not progress.

BUILT ON THE GRAPH — no new registry (BEB-2071/2484). Go

DIRECTIVE — Alex, 2026-08-25. MANAGER WIRING + THE VISUAL PROOF DEBT. Extends 65220.

PART 1 — WIRE THE MANAGER TO EVERYTHING. A manager that reads counters only is half a manager. It needs all four, read AND write:
1) BOTH GRAPHS — the service graph (BEB-2484) and the client/touch graph (BEB-2069/2070). Nodes and edges, read and touch. Blocked on GRAPH_WRITE_TOKEN (65219).
2) TICKETS — read, comment, set weight, front to 10, escalate. That is its authority per 65220.
3) DOCS — BB Docs read and write. Findings, batches and evidence land as docs, not as bridge prose. Bridge prose is never canonical.
4) VIZ OUTPUT ORDERS, DIRECT — the manager ORDERS a render/recording itself: screenshot_url, record_url, contract_run. It does not ask a build lane to schedule proof. It orders it and the artefact comes back to it.

PART 2 — THE PROOF DEBT. Alex has never seen the visual proof. He is owed ONE PER COMPLETED TASK — thousands, against 1,139 done. The visual proof law (real browser render + recording → R2 → linked on the ticket) has been law since the beginning and has not been honoured. m2535 and the 2026-08-03 ruling are explicit: Alex is NEVER the tester and NEVER the recorder. SpecOps tests it as designed and PRODUCES the recording itself; the contract_run verdict per element plus the video, delivered into BB Docs, IS the deliverable. Alex watches it there.

REQUIRED:
A) FORWARD, NO EXCEPTIONS — from now, no ticket reaches done without its recording linked. Already enforced at the front by T1 source-block; this is the same rule at the exit.
B) BACKFILL THE DEBT — every completed task gets its proof produced. Do not hand-run this: the manager orders the renders in batches, continuously, until the debt is zero. Report it as a burndown number every wake: proofs owed, proofs produced, remaining.
C) ONE PLACE TO WATCH — a BB Docs index, newest first, every completed task with its verdict and its recording, one click each. Alex should not hunt across tickets to see his own proo

DIRECTIVE — Alex, 2026-08-25. ASST MANAGER. Supersedes the manager design in 65220/65222 — smaller, simpler, runs more often. Build this instead.

WHAT IT IS: the three missing verbs bolted onto the wake ladder that already exists (BEB-3622, done — predicates S1..S4, wake_record, get_state). NOT a new system, NOT a new store, NOT a new worker. The ladder has SENSE and RECORD. It is missing DIFF, DRILL, ORDER — so a blocked step gets recorded and then nothing happens. That is exactly last night: S1 unsatisfied, correctly refused, waited 14 hours.

THE DEFECT IT REMOVES: the wake engine is four ways to REFUSE with no way to ACT. Alex's 08-22 law — a fix removes a way to wait, it does not add a way to refuse.

THE THREE VERBS. Every one takes a node id, so goals, causes, tickets and services are addressed identically. No handler per thing.

DIFF — compare this tick's vector to the one stored last tick. Alarm on the DERIVATIVE, not the level: a counter that did not move, or a shape identical on an empty pass and a healthy one (BEB-2690 §3, fired 3× today, nobody acted). Missing or stale numbers ARE the red; do not wait for a red to be filed.

DRILL — why(node) returns cause + attempt count + raw last error in ONE hop. If diagnosing needs three tickets or a log dive, the asst manager cannot do it on a tick. This is the piece with no equivalent today and it is what would have said at 03:00 why 560 deploys failed.

ORDER — four actions, nothing else: FRONT (weight 10 to the head, timestamped, with reason), RENDER (screenshot_url/record_url/contract_run, ordered directly), HEAL (self_heal on the signature), DEMAND-EMIT (name the service that owes a per-pass number). It never builds. It never blocks.

CADENCE: runs on the tick, far more often than a wake. Cheap by construction — one SENSE call, one DIFF against stored state, and it only DRILLs when DIFF alarms.

WIRING: both graphs (BEB-2484 service, BEB-2069/2070 touch), tickets, BB Docs, viz orders direct. Blocked on GRAPH

DIRECTIVE — Alex, 2026-08-25. GRAPH TOKEN IS SYSTEM CONFIG, NOT A HUNT.

Alex's ruling: the graph service DB and the memory DB are SYSTEM. Nobody should be finding tokens or writing files to make them work. A binding that has to be located by hand is the defect.

1) NO HUNTING. GRAPH_WRITE_TOKEN is not a secret to go looking for — the value already exists in the vault (graph:write:dispatcher, len 64). The dispatcher must READ IT FROM THE VAULT at runtime like every other system credential. If the vault read path does not exist for workers, that gap IS the deliverable.

2) NO FILE WRITING. Do not solve this with a wrangler secret, a .dev.vars, a hardcoded value, or any file. Per SETTINGS FIRST (BEB-3851): every value that can block the loop is a settings row, flippable on the tick in cloud, never a code change or a deploy.

3) SYSTEM WIRING, ONCE. Graph service DB and memory DB are core system stores. Their credentials wire at deploy from the vault, for every worker that needs them, automatically. Not per-worker, not per-incident, not a button Alex presses. If Alex has to press anything for a system store to work, that is the bug, not the fix.

4) FAIL LOUD MEANWHILE. Per 65217A, a worker that cannot read a system store credential REFUSES TO RUN and says which store and which credential by name. It does not start up and silently no-op, which is how the dispatcher wrote zero graph nodes for weeks without anyone knowing.

I withdraw the ask for Alex to set a worker secret. Wire it from the vault.

CLOSES ON: dispatcher writes a graph node and reads it back, with GRAPH_WRITE_TOKEN never appearing in a file or a manual command; and a worker started without a system store credential refuses and names it.
